issues.title: TypeLoadException at boot after a mod or Harmony update
issues.explanation: A mod was built against a different Harmony version than the one loaded, so its assembly fails to load and every def and feature it adds disappears. This often cascades into many unrelated-looking errors.
issues.fix: Make sure Harmony (brrainz.harmony) and the named mod are both up to date, and that only one copy of Harmony is active. Remove any old mod that ships its own 0Harmony.dll.

issues.title: A mod's whole assembly failed to load (getting types in assembly)
issues.explanation: RimWorld could not read the types in a mod's compiled code, so the entire mod is disabled. Every def it defines then fails with 'is not a def type' or 'could not find type', which looks like dozens of separate XML errors but has one cause.
issues.fix: Look earlier in the log for the first 'ReflectionTypeLoadException getting types in assembly' line: it names the failing mod. Update that mod and its dependencies (especially Harmony), confirm required mods are active, and make sure it supports your RimWorld version.

issues.title: Tried to use an uninitialized DefOf
issues.explanation: A mod read a shortcut to a def (a DefOf) before defs finished loading, so the value was empty. Usually a startup-timing bug in the mod, and the feature that needed it will not work.
issues.fix: Update the named mod; this is an author-side timing bug. If it only appears with another mod present, a load-order or patch conflict is exposing it. Report the exact message to the author.

keywords: tried to use an uninitialized defof

issues.title: A mod's startup code threw an error
issues.explanation: A mod's start-of-game initialization (its static constructor) threw, so part or all of that mod is left half-set-up. This commonly breaks one feature while the rest of the mod appears to work.
issues.fix: Find the mod in the stack trace, update it, and confirm its required mods are active and in the right order. If it started after a game update, the mod likely needs a version bump. Report the trace to the author.

issues.title: Error during map generation (background thread)
issues.explanation: Something threw while a map was being generated on a background thread. Map generation runs mod code (GenSteps, scatterers, faction and terrain logic), so a mod feeding it bad data can abort the new map or leave it incomplete.
issues.fix: Note which mod appears in the trace and disable it to confirm. Generating a fresh map, or changing the biome or scenario, sometimes avoids the specific data that triggers it. Report the trace to the author.

issues.title: Method not found (a library version mismatch)
issues.explanation: Code called a method that does not exist in the loaded version of a library or another mod. This almost always means two mods expect different versions of the same code, or a mod is older or newer than the game.
issues.fix: Update the game, the named mod, and any shared libraries it uses (Harmony, VEF, HugsLib, etc.) so they all match. If the trace mentions another mod's type, update or remove the older of the two.

issues.title: A mod's XML patch could not find its target
issues.explanation: A mod tried to edit game data at a location (an XPath) that no longer exists, so the change never happened. The most common causes are a game update that moved the data, or another mod that changed it first.
issues.fix: This is usually a load-order or compatibility issue for the named mod. Update it, adjust load order, or report the exact XPath to the author. It is safe to keep playing, but the patched feature is missing.

issues.title: A mod sets an XML field the game no longer has
issues.explanation: A def or patch sets a field that does not exist on that type, so the value is ignored. After a RimWorld update this usually means the field was renamed or removed and the mod has not caught up.
issues.fix: Update the named mod to a version made for your RimWorld version. If none exists, the setting simply does nothing; it will not crash your game. Report the field name to the author.

issues.title: A saved reference could not be found when loading
issues.explanation: While loading a save, the game could not find something it had a reference to. On an existing save this almost always means a mod that was present before is now missing, disabled, or changed.
issues.fix: Re-add or re-enable the mod that was removed or updated since the save was made, then load again. If you meant to remove it, expect the content it added to be gone. The Mods changed indicator lists what changed since this save.

keywords: could not load reference to object with loadid
could not resolve reference to object with loadid

issues.title: A mod's settings failed to load or save
issues.explanation: A mod threw while reading or writing its own settings. The setting may reset to default, and on load an older settings file can be incompatible with a newer version of the mod.
issues.fix: Open the mod's settings once and re-apply your choices, or delete its config file in the Config folder to reset it. If it persists after an update, report the trace to the author.

issues.title: Error while drawing a pawn
issues.explanation: A mod's rendering code threw while drawing a pawn, so the pawn may flicker, render wrong, or spam this error every frame, which hurts FPS. Body, hair, apparel and gene rendering mods are the usual sources.
issues.fix: Find the mod in the trace, update it, and check for known incompatibilities with other body or apparel mods. Disabling render-related mods one at a time confirms the culprit.

issues.title: Out of memory
issues.explanation: The game ran out of memory, usually from too many large-texture mods loaded at once rather than any single bug. RimWorld will become unstable and can crash.
issues.fix: Reduce the number of texture-heavy mods, add a texture-optimizing or performance mod, and make sure you are running the 64-bit game. Restarting RimWorld between long sessions also helps.

issues.title: Stack overflow (infinite loop in code)
issues.explanation: Code called itself without stopping until it ran out of stack space. In modding this is often two mods patching the same method so each keeps calling the other, and it can crash the game with no clean error.
issues.fix: Note the two mods that repeat in the trace and disable one to confirm the loop. Report the pair to both authors; there is no user-side fix beyond removing one of them.

issues.title: A def could not be built because its type is missing
issues.explanation: XML tried to create a def of a class that is not loaded, so the item, building or feature it describes never appears. The class belongs to a mod that failed to load or is not installed.
issues.fix: This is usually a downstream symptom: a required mod is missing or a mod's code failed to load earlier. Install and activate the mod that provides the class, and fix any assembly-load error higher up in the log first.
